summary: A local meeting-notes app for your Mac: a menu bar button records system audio and your microphone, whisper.cpp transcribes on your machine, an LLM turns the transcript plus your rough notes into a summary with decisions and action items, and everything lands as Markdown files in a folder you own. Nothing leaves the machine except the optional LLM call.

stack.why: system audio capture is a native API; wrapping it in Electron is where these projects stall

stack.choice: ScreenCaptureKit for system audio, AVAudioEngine for the mic
stack.why: no virtual audio driver to install, and two separate taps you can mix
local, free, good enough on Apple Silicon

stack.choice: An LLM API behind a small provider interface
stack.why: the one network call, swappable and optional
greppable, portable, no index to corrupt

prerequisites.name: A Mac with Apple Silicon running macOS 14 or newer
prerequisites.why: ScreenCaptureKit audio capture needs macOS 13+, and local transcription is only pleasant on Apple Silicon.
prerequisites.get: Apple menu > About This Mac. Update through System Settings > General > Software Update if below 14.

prerequisites.name: Xcode 16 or newer
prerequisites.why: Swift, SwiftUI and the macOS SDK come with it. The Command Line Tools alone are not enough for a signed menu bar app.
prerequisites.get: Install from the Mac App Store (it is large; start the download first). Open it once to accept the licence and install components.

prerequisites.name: Homebrew, cmake and ffmpeg
prerequisites.why: cmake builds whisper.cpp; ffmpeg is the easiest way to inspect and convert audio while you debug Phase 1.
prerequisites.get: Install Homebrew from brew.sh, then: brew install cmake ffmpeg

prerequisites.name: whisper.cpp built from source
prerequisites.why: The whisper-cli binary is what Phase 2 shells out to.
prerequisites.get: git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp && cd whisper.cpp && cmake -B build && cmake --build build --config Release. The binary is build/bin/whisper-cli.

prerequisites.name: The medium.en whisper model (about 1.5 GB)
prerequisites.why: Without a model file there is no transcription. medium.en is the quality-speed balance for English meetings.
prerequisites.get: Inside the whisper.cpp folder: ./models/download-ggml-model.sh medium.en. It saves to models/ggml-medium.en.bin. Use small.en (about 500 MB) if disk or speed is tight.

prerequisites.name: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic)
prerequisites.why: Phase 3 sends the transcript to a model for the summary. Without a key the app still records and transcribes; it just skips the summary.
prerequisites.get: Anthropic: console.anthropic.com > API Keys > Create Key. OpenAI: platform.openai.com/api-keys > Create new secret key. Copy it once; it is not shown again. Put it in .env, never in the source.
prerequisites.cost: pay per use; a one-hour meeting summary costs a few cents

prerequisites.name: A Groq or OpenAI key for hosted transcription
prerequisites.why: An optional fast path when local transcription is too slow on your machine. Local stays the default.
prerequisites.get: Groq: console.groq.com > API Keys. OpenAI: the same key as above works for the audio endpoint.
prerequisites.cost: pay per use; Groq has a free tier

prerequisites.name: Screen Recording and Microphone permissions
prerequisites.why: System audio arrives under the Screen Recording permission (no separate audio permission exists); the mic needs its own. Both are granted once per app build.
prerequisites.get: macOS prompts on first use. If you dismiss the prompt, the app must be relaunched before it can ask again; otherwise System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and > Microphone.

env.name: NOTES_DIR
env.where: Where meeting folders are written. Any folder you sync or back up.

env.name: WHISPER_BIN
env.where: Path to the binary you built.

env.name: WHISPER_MODEL
env.where: Path to the model you downloaded.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env.where: Anthropic console. Leave empty to skip summaries.

env.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
env.where: OpenAI dashboard. Used for summaries if no Anthropic key, and for hosted Whisper if enabled.

env.name: LLM_MODEL
env.where: Model name for summaries. Anything the provider offers.

env.name: GROQ_API_KEY
env.where: console.groq.com. Enables the hosted transcription fast path.

env.name: TRANSCRIBE_MODE
env.where: local or hosted. Local is the default and works offline.

phases.title: Audio capture, proven as a CLI first
phases.goal: Before any UI exists, prove you can record system audio and the mic into a WAV that whisper-cli accepts. This is the phase that kills the project if skipped.

steps.do: Create an Xcode project with two targets: a command-line tool and the menu bar app
steps.detail: The CLI target is for this phase; the app target waits until Phase 5. Both share a Swift package with the capture code.

steps.do: Capture system audio with ScreenCaptureKit
steps.detail: Build an SCStreamConfiguration with capturesAudio true. SCStream still requires a screen output to be added even for audio only: add one and set minimumFrameInterval to a very large value so no real frames are processed. On macOS 14.2+ you may instead use Core Audio process taps (AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap) for genuine audio-only capture; pick one and say which in a comment.

steps.do: Capture the microphone with AVAudioEngine, separately
steps.detail: Do not use SCStreamConfiguration's microphone capture; it has known output-corruption reports. Tap the input node and collect buffers.

steps.do: Mix both taps and write 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM WAV
steps.detail: Resample explicitly with AVAudioConverter. Not 44.1 kHz, not float, not stereo. whisper-cli accepts 16-bit WAV only; every hour lost to this project is lost here.

steps.do: Run the CLI for 30 seconds while music plays and you speak

check: afinfo reports 16000 Hz, 1 channel, 16-bit for the WAV
Playing the WAV back you hear both the music and your voice
whisper-cli accepts the file without a format error and prints text
Denying Screen Recording produces a clear error naming the System Settings pane, not a silent empty file
traps: Do not tell the user to install BlackHole or Loopback. ScreenCaptureKit delivers system audio under the screen-recording grant with no driver.
The permission prompt appears once per launch. If it is dismissed the app must be relaunched; detect the denied state and say so.

phases.title: Transcription
phases.goal: A transcript from a WAV, local by default, with progress you can see and a hosted fast path when a key exists.

steps.do: Shell out to whisper-cli with -otxt
steps.detail: Process with WHISPER_BIN, WHISPER_MODEL and the audio path. Read the .txt it writes. Capture stderr for progress lines.

steps.do: Report progress
steps.detail: A 45-minute meeting on the medium model is minutes of CPU. Parse whisper's progress output into a percentage; a UI that looks frozen will be assumed broken.

steps.do: Add the hosted path behind TRANSCRIBE_MODE
steps.detail: When hosted and a Groq or OpenAI key exists, post the WAV to the Whisper endpoint. Local remains the default: the recording should not leave the machine unless asked.

steps.do: Make it resumable
steps.detail: Write the transcript to a temp name and rename on completion. Killing the app mid-transcription must leave the audio intact and no half-written transcript.

check: A 5-minute recording produces a transcript whose first and last sentences are recognisably correct
Progress moves during transcription
Killing the app mid-transcription leaves audio.wav intact and no transcript.txt
With TRANSCRIBE_MODE=hosted and a key, the same file transcribes via the API

phases.title: Summarization
phases.goal: A fixed prompt turns the transcript and your jotted notes into a 5-bullet summary, decisions and action items with owners, and long meetings are chunked rather than truncated.

steps.do: Write the provider interface and one implementation
steps.detail: summarize(transcript, notes) returning structured text. Anthropic first; OpenAI as a second implementation selected by which key exists.

steps.do: Chunk transcripts that exceed the context window
steps.detail: Split on paragraph boundaries into chunks under the model's limit, summarize each, then summarize the summaries. Never silently truncate: that produces confident notes about the first third of a meeting.

steps.do: Pass the user's rough notes alongside the transcript
steps.detail: This is the actual Granola idea: your jottings steer what the summary emphasises.

check: A transcript with three clear decisions and two assigned tasks yields notes naming all five
A 90-minute transcript summarizes without an API error
With no key present the step is skipped with a clear note in the output, not an error

phases.title: Notes on disk
phases.goal: One folder per meeting, plain Markdown with frontmatter, never overwriting.

steps.do: Write NOTES_DIR/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>/ with audio.wav, transcript.txt and notes.md
steps.detail: notes.md: YAML frontmatter (title, date, duration, participants, model), the summary, a divider, then the full transcript.

steps.do: Derive the title from the summary and never overwrite
steps.detail: If the folder exists, suffix a counter. Two meetings in the same minute must produce two folders.

check: Two meetings started in the same minute produce two folders
notes.md opens correctly in a plain Markdown editor with no app running
The audio file is kept next to the notes

phases.title: Menu bar app
phases.goal: Start and stop from the menu bar, jot notes while recording, see recent meetings, and get told exactly what to do when a permission is missing.

steps.do: Build the MenuBarExtra with Start/Stop and elapsed time
steps.detail: A recording indicator that is unmistakable. Wire the capture code from Phase 1.

steps.do: Add the live jot-notes field
steps.detail: Text typed during the meeting is passed to the summarizer in Phase 3.

steps.do: List recent meetings with Reveal in Finder
steps.detail: Read NOTES_DIR; newest first.

steps.do: Handle permissions explicitly
steps.detail: If Screen Recording or Microphone is denied, show which System Settings pane to open and the relaunch caveat, instead of failing silently.

check: A full meeting runs start to notes without touching a terminal
First launch on a machine that has never granted permission explains itself
The jotted notes visibly influence the summary

phases.title: Offline, packaging, README
phases.goal: Works with the network off when the model is present, signed for your own machine, documented.

steps.do: Test with Wi-Fi off and no LLM key
steps.detail: Transcript saved; summary skipped with an honest note in notes.md.

steps.do: Sign locally and document the Gatekeeper first-run step
steps.detail: Sign with your development certificate for your own use. Right-click > Open the first time.

steps.do: Write the README
steps.detail: Permissions and where to grant them, model download size, disk cost per hour of audio, and a plain warning that recording a meeting can require consent from everyone in it depending on where they are.

check: Airplane mode produces a complete transcript and a note saying the summary was skipped
A fresh Mac goes from clone to first recording using only the README

phases.title: Distribute it
phases.goal: Only for the product path: an app other people can install without terrifying Gatekeeper dialogs, that updates itself, and that tells you when it crashes.

steps.do: Join the Apple Developer Program and sign with a Developer ID
steps.detail: Required to notarize. Xcode > Signing & Capabilities with the Developer ID Application certificate.

steps.do: Add Sparkle for updates
steps.detail: Host an appcast XML on your domain; sign updates with the EdDSA key Sparkle generates.

steps.do: Add opt-in crash reporting
steps.detail: A local crash log the user can send you, or Sentry's macOS SDK behind an explicit opt-in toggle. Never on by default for a privacy-first app.

check: A notarized build opens on a second Mac with no right-click workaround
Publishing a new appcast entry makes the installed app offer the update
A deliberate crash produces a report only when the toggle is on

product.outcome: A privacy-first meeting notes app you could hand to colleagues: notarized, self-updating, local by default, with a clear consent posture.

architecture.owns: ScreenCaptureKit and AVAudioEngine taps, mixing, WAV writing
architecture.swap: Core Audio process taps on 14.2+, or any source producing 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV
WhisperKit in-process, or any engine writing the same transcript.txt

architecture.owns: the provider interface, chunking, the fixed prompt
architecture.swap: Any LLM provider; local models via Ollama behind the same interface

architecture.owns: the meeting folder layout and frontmatter
architecture.swap: Obsidian-compatible folder; a sync tool sits outside the app
The only SwiftUI code; everything else is a package

operations.backup: NOTES_DIR is plain files: point Time Machine, iCloud Drive or Syncthing at it. The app holds no other state.
operations.restore: Copy the folder back. The recent-meetings list is derived from the folder, so there is nothing else to restore.
operations.monitoring: For a distributed app: opt-in crash reports and an update-check success rate from the appcast host's logs.
operations.incident: If an API key is leaked, rotate it at the provider and ship a release that clears the stored key. If a transcription bug corrupts notes, the audio.wav next to each note allows regeneration.

releaseGate: A notarized build installs and records on a Mac that has never had the developer tools
The consent warning is in the README and the first-run screen
One update delivered through Sparkle to a real install

notIncluded: Sync across devices and a mobile app. That is most of the subscription.
Automatic calendar joining and bot attendees.
Someone else's servers and support when a recording is lost.
after: Speaker diarization with a local model so action items get real owners
Ollama as a local summarizer behind the same provider interface for a fully offline pipeline
